item.research_question: Can a Ti–Zr–Nb–Ta–Ag high-entropy alloy (HEA) processed via mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering (SPS) exhibit superior mechanical properties and corrosion resistance in artificial saliva compared to commercial Ti6Al4V for dental implant applications?
item.material_system: Ti–Zr–Nb–Ta–Ag HEA (35% Ti, 35% Zr, 20% Nb, 5% Ta, 5% Ag atomic %) and commercial Ti6Al4V
item.processing_route: High-energy ball milling (300 rpm, 20 h, WC vials/balls, argon atmosphere) followed by spark plasma sintering (1200 °C, 50 MPa, 10 min, 200 °C/min heating rate, vacuum ~5 × 10⁻² mbar)
item.test_conditions: In vitro corrosion tests in artificial saliva (Fusayama–Meyer type) at pH 3.0, 4.9, and 6.8; microindentation (100 mN load); electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (1 kHz to 1 mHz); potentiodynamic polarization (+250 mV to −2000 mV vs Ag/AgCl); XPS; contact angle measurements
key_findings: The SPS-processed HEA exhibited a hardness of 8.2 GPa, nearly double that of Ti6Al4V (4.11 GPa).
The resistance to plastic deformation (H³/E²) for the HEA was 0.0312 GPa, significantly higher than 0.00349 GPa for Ti6Al4V.
The HEA showed the highest charge transfer resistance (Rct) of 1.0805 × 10⁷ Ω⋅cm² at pH 6.8, compared to Ti6Al4V.
The double-layer constant phase element (CPEdl) value for the HEA was 0.085 µF⁻¹⋅cm⁻²⋅sⁿ, indicating a more stable passive film.
Corrosion current density (icorr) for the HEA declined by at least one order of magnitude compared to Ti6Al4V at all pH levels.
XPS analysis confirmed the formation of biocompatible surface oxides including TiO₂, ZrO₂, Nb₂O₅, Ta₂O₅, and metallic Ag.
The HEA surface was moderately hydrophobic with a contact angle of 83.9° for water, compared to 65.41° for Ti6Al4V.
The HEA microstructure consisted of dual BCC phases (BCC1, BCC2) and an ultrafine Zr-based phase with crystallite sizes of 21.7 nm, 15.8 nm, and 23 nm respectively.
item.mechanism: The superior mechanical properties are attributed to refined microstructure, multicomponent alloying effects, solid-solution strengthening, and grain boundary strengthening resulting from severe plastic deformation during ball milling and controlled recrystallization during SPS. The enhanced corrosion resistance is due to the formation of a compact, inert, and stable passive film composed of TiO₂, ZrO₂, Nb₂O₅, and Ta₂O₅, which effectively impedes charge transfer and protects the matrix, particularly in acidic environments where Ti6Al4V films degrade.
item.limitations: The elastic modulus of the HEA (~132 GPa) is slightly higher than commercially pure titanium (~110 GPa), which may lead to stress shielding, although it is lower than Co–Cr and stainless steel alloys.
item.future_work: Future work should focus on optimizing the elastic modulus and reducing potential stress shielding through compositional adjustments (e.g., increasing β-phase stabilizing elements) and introducing controlled porosity via advanced processing strategies.
quotes: The HEA exhibits nearly double the hardness (8.2 GPa) and significantly higher resistance to plastic deformation (H³/E² =0.0312 GPa) compared to Ti6Al4V
The HEA exhibited the highest charge transfer resistance (1.0805 × 107 ℧⋅cm²) and the lowest double-layer constant phase element value (0.085 µ℧⁻¹⋅cm⁻²⋅sn)
Future work should focus on further optimizing the elastic modulus and reducing potential stress shielding. This may be achieved through compositional adjustments

item.research_question: To evaluate the potential of a Ti-Zr-Nb-Ta-Ag high entropy alloy synthesized via mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering for dental bioimplant applications, specifically regarding its phase composition, microstructure, mechanical properties, surface characteristics, and corrosion resistance.
item.processing_route: Mechanical alloying followed by Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS)
item.test_conditions: In vitro corrosion testing in artificial saliva at acidic pH; microhardness measurement; XPS surface characterization
key_findings: The SPS process resulted in a homogeneous microstructure with dual phases: BCC structure and an equiaxed Zr-rich phase.
The microhardness of the SPS-ed HEA was 8.2 GPa, nearly double that of Ti6Al4V (4.11 GPa).
XPS analysis revealed the formation of surface oxides including TiO2, ZrO2, Nb2O5, and Ta2O5 alongside Ag.
The SPSed HEA outperformed Ti6Al4V in corrosion resistance in artificial saliva, showing higher impedance values and lower corrosion current densities even at acidic pH.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the suitability of the material to the combination of its mechanical strength (derived from the dual-phase microstructure) and enhanced in vitro corrosion resistance (due to the formation of protective surface oxides).
item.future_work: Future studies should focus on the in vivo evaluation and long-term performance assessment of the developed HEA under real oral conditions.
quotes: This study reports the synthesis of Ti-Zr-Nb-Ta-Ag HEA via mechanical alloying and SPS and evaluates its potential for dental bioimplant applications.
The micro hardness of SPS-ed HEA is 8.2 GPa, nearly double that of Ti6Al4V (4.11 GPa).

In vitro corrosion testing results in artificial saliva confirmed that the SPSed HEA alloy outperformed Ti6Al4V in terms of corrosion resistance, even at acidic pH, by showing higher impedance values and lower corrosion current densities.
